In addition to knowledge domains, psychological factors such as self-efficacy and teaching beliefs are critical determinants of technol- ogy adoption. Teachers’ self-efficacy can be defined as a subjective assessment of their own teaching ability \[[10\]](#6-conclusion). It reflects their positive expectations of the teaching process and outcomes, which in turn in- fluence their teaching behaviors and students’ learning outcomes \[[11\]](#11-klassen-rm-tze-vm-teachers-self-efficacy-personality-and-teaching-effective--28-czocher-ja-melhuish-k-kandasamy-ss-building-mathematics-self-efficacy-of-ness-a-meta-analysis-educ-res-rev-2014125976-httpdxdoiorg101016-stem-undergraduates-through-mathematical-modelling-internat-j-math-ed-sci). Teaching beliefs represent the fundamental tenets and values that educators internalize regarding the objectives of education, the learning process, the characteristics of learners, and the content and method- ologies of teaching \[[12\]](#11-klassen-rm-tze-vm-teachers-self-efficacy-personality-and-teaching-effective--28-czocher-ja-melhuish-k-kandasamy-ss-building-mathematics-self-efficacy-of-ness-a-meta-analysis-educ-res-rev-2014125976-httpdxdoiorg101016-stem-undergraduates-through-mathematical-modelling-internat-j-math-ed-sci). Teaching beliefs constitute the foundation of a teacher’s educational philosophy and practice, and they shape the teacher’s educational conduct \[[13\]](#11-klassen-rm-tze-vm-teachers-self-efficacy-personality-and-teaching-effective--28-czocher-ja-melhuish-k-kandasamy-ss-building-mathematics-self-efficacy-of-ness-a-meta-analysis-educ-res-rev-2014125976-httpdxdoiorg101016-stem-undergraduates-through-mathematical-modelling-internat-j-math-ed-sci). Teachers who exhibit high levels of teacher self-efficacy and teaching beliefs are more likely to demonstrate confidence in exploring and implementing elements of the AI-TPACK framework \[[14–18\]](#11-klassen-rm-tze-vm-teachers-self-efficacy-personality-and-teaching-effective--28-czocher-ja-melhuish-k-kandasamy-ss-building-mathematics-self-efficacy-of-ness-a-meta-analysis-educ-res-rev-2014125976-httpdxdoiorg101016-stem-undergraduates-through-mathematical-modelling-internat-j-math-ed-sci).

While generic AI-TPACK frameworks have emerged recently \[[2\]](#6-conclusion), they often treat pedagogical content knowledge as a universal con- struct, ignoring the discipline-specific nuances of mathematics educa- tion. In addition to bridge the gap in existing literature, we also focus specifically on AI-TPACK readiness. While AI-TPACK refers to the static knowledge components, ‘‘readiness’’ represents a more active state of preparation for future technology integration. For pre-service teachers like MTES, who are moving from university learning to professional work, AI-TPACK readiness means more than just knowing AI tools. It also includes their perceived ability and psychological willingness to use these tools within the strict logical rules of mathematics education. Therefore, this study aims to: (1) develop and validate a domain- specific AI-TPACK scale for MTES; (2) examine the current status of AI-TPACK readiness across grade levels; and (3) utilize structural equation modeling (SEM) to explore the interplay between self-efficacy, teaching beliefs, and AI-TPACK domains. By providing evidence-based insights, this research contributes to the global discourse on teacher preparation and the digital transformation of mathematics education. So in order to better enhance the AI-TPACK competence of MTES, the paper was based on three key research questions:

- RQ1: What is the current status of AI-TPACK readiness among Chinese MTES ?
- RQ2: Are there significant differences in AI-TPACK readiness, self- efficacy, and teaching beliefs across different grade levels of MTES within the Chinese teacher education curriculum?
- RQ3: How do self-efficacy and teaching beliefs predict AI-TPACK readiness among MTES, and what is the structural relationship between these constructs?

This study makes several significant contributions to the field of teacher education. First, it addresses the urgent need for a domain- specific AI-TPACK framework tailored to mathematics education, mov- ing beyond generic technology models to account for the unique log- ical and rigorous demands of the discipline. Second, by integrating self-efficacy and teaching beliefs as core determinants, the research provides a more holistic understanding of teacher readiness that en- compasses both technical proficiency and psychological disposition. Third, through the empirical testing of structural relationships, this study uncovers the mediated pathways of AI-TPACK development, of- fering evidence-based insights for the redesign of mathematics teacher training programs in the AI era.

## 2. Literature review

### _2.1._ _From_ _TPACK_ _to_ _AI-TPACK_ _in_ _mathematics_ _education_

TPACK framework serves as a foundational model for understanding how teachers integrate technology into their instructional practice \[[19\]](#11-klassen-rm-tze-vm-teachers-self-efficacy-personality-and-teaching-effective--28-czocher-ja-melhuish-k-kandasamy-ss-building-mathematics-self-efficacy-of-ness-a-meta-analysis-educ-res-rev-2014125976-httpdxdoiorg101016-stem-undergraduates-through-mathematical-modelling-internat-j-math-ed-sci) proposed the Technological Pedagogical Content Knowledge (TPACK) framework, which has since become a significant theoretical framework 

in the field of education \[[20\]](#11-klassen-rm-tze-vm-teachers-self-efficacy-personality-and-teaching-effective--28-czocher-ja-melhuish-k-kandasamy-ss-building-mathematics-self-efficacy-of-ness-a-meta-analysis-educ-res-rev-2014125976-httpdxdoiorg101016-stem-undergraduates-through-mathematical-modelling-internat-j-math-ed-sci). As shown in [Fig. 1(](#fig-2-mtess-ai-tpack-research-framework)a), TPACK describes a framework for teachers to combine Technological Knowledge (TK), Pedagogical Knowledge (PK), and Content Knowledge (CK) to facili- tate effective teaching practices. Technological Pedagogical Knowledge (TPK) represents The combination of technology and pedagogy. Tech- nological Content Knowledge (TCK) represents the interdisciplinary field concerned with the integration of technology and content. PCK represents the integration of pedagogical and content knowledge. The combination of these components constitutes the TPACK \[[19\]](#11-klassen-rm-tze-vm-teachers-self-efficacy-personality-and-teaching-effective--28-czocher-ja-melhuish-k-kandasamy-ss-building-mathematics-self-efficacy-of-ness-a-meta-analysis-educ-res-rev-2014125976-httpdxdoiorg101016-stem-undergraduates-through-mathematical-modelling-internat-j-math-ed-sci). However, the emergence of artificial intelligence necessitates a re-evaluation of these intersections(see [Fig. 1(](#fig-2-mtess-ai-tpack-research-framework)b)). Unlike traditional digital tools, AI introduces autonomous and adaptive capabilities that transform the ‘‘T’’ (Technology) within the framework into a more dynamic and interactive component. In the specific context of math- ematics education, this evolution means that AI-TK (AI-Technological Knowledge) is no longer just about operating software, but about un- derstanding algorithmic logic and its potential to scaffold mathematical reasoning \[[21\]](#11-klassen-rm-tze-vm-teachers-self-efficacy-personality-and-teaching-effective--28-czocher-ja-melhuish-k-kandasamy-ss-building-mathematics-self-efficacy-of-ness-a-meta-analysis-educ-res-rev-2014125976-httpdxdoiorg101016-stem-undergraduates-through-mathematical-modelling-internat-j-math-ed-sci). The transition from TPACK to AI-TPACK reflects a shift where AI acts as a ‘‘pedagogical partner’’ that can visualize abstract structures and provide personalized learning trajectories \[[22,23\]](#11-klassen-rm-tze-vm-teachers-self-efficacy-personality-and-teaching-effective--28-czocher-ja-melhuish-k-kandasamy-ss-building-mathematics-self-efficacy-of-ness-a-meta-analysis-educ-res-rev-2014125976-httpdxdoiorg101016-stem-undergraduates-through-mathematical-modelling-internat-j-math-ed-sci). This structural evolution is particularly critical for MTES, who must navi- gate the convergence of rigid mathematical rigor and the open-ended possibilities of generative AI \[[24,25\]](#11-klassen-rm-tze-vm-teachers-self-efficacy-personality-and-teaching-effective--28-czocher-ja-melhuish-k-kandasamy-ss-building-mathematics-self-efficacy-of-ness-a-meta-analysis-educ-res-rev-2014125976-httpdxdoiorg101016-stem-undergraduates-through-mathematical-modelling-internat-j-math-ed-sci).

### _2.2._ _Self-efficacy_ _and_ _teaching_ _beliefs_ _in_ _AI-TPACK_

A critical contribution of this research is the integration of psy- chological constructs into the AI-TPACK framework, moving beyond a purely cognitive knowledge-based model. Self-efficacy, defined as an individual’s belief in their capability to execute specific tasks, serves as a vital psychological catalyst in the adoption of complex AI tools \[[26\]](#11-klassen-rm-tze-vm-teachers-self-efficacy-personality-and-teaching-effective--28-czocher-ja-melhuish-k-kandasamy-ss-building-mathematics-self-efficacy-of-ness-a-meta-analysis-educ-res-rev-2014125976-httpdxdoiorg101016-stem-undergraduates-through-mathematical-modelling-internat-j-math-ed-sci). For MTES, high levels of self-efficacy reduce the perceived complexity of AI systems, allowing them to persist through the technical challenges of integrating intelligent tutoring or dynamic geometry software into their instruction \[[27,28\]](#11-klassen-rm-tze-vm-teachers-self-efficacy-personality-and-teaching-effective--28-czocher-ja-melhuish-k-kandasamy-ss-building-mathematics-self-efficacy-of-ness-a-meta-analysis-educ-res-rev-2014125976-httpdxdoiorg101016-stem-undergraduates-through-mathematical-modelling-internat-j-math-ed-sci).

Complementing self-efficacy, teaching beliefs act as a cognitive filter through which new technologies are evaluated and implemented. According to Liljedahl et al. \[[29\]](#11-klassen-rm-tze-vm-teachers-self-efficacy-personality-and-teaching-effective--28-czocher-ja-melhuish-k-kandasamy-ss-building-mathematics-self-efficacy-of-ness-a-meta-analysis-educ-res-rev-2014125976-httpdxdoiorg101016-stem-undergraduates-through-mathematical-modelling-internat-j-math-ed-sci), the pedagogical orientation of pre- service teachers significantly dictates their perceived usefulness of tech- nology. In mathematics education, these beliefs often center on the bal- ance between teacher-led procedural instruction and student-centered conceptual exploration \[[30,31\]](#11-klassen-rm-tze-vm-teachers-self-efficacy-personality-and-teaching-effective--28-czocher-ja-melhuish-k-kandasamy-ss-building-mathematics-self-efficacy-of-ness-a-meta-analysis-educ-res-rev-2014125976-httpdxdoiorg101016-stem-undergraduates-through-mathematical-modelling-internat-j-math-ed-sci). Within the AI-TPACK structure, teach- ing beliefs determine whether a teacher views AI as a tool for reinforc- ing traditional rote learning or as a medium for fostering high-order thinking. This psychological layer is essential for understanding why teachers with similar technical knowledge (AI-TK) may exhibit vastly different levels of instructional readiness (AI-TPACK).

### _2.3._ _AI_ _in_ _mathematics_ _teacher_ _education_ _in_ _China_

Mathematics teacher preparation in China is situated within a unique cultural and high-stakes environment \[[8,](#6-conclusion)[32\]](#11-klassen-rm-tze-vm-teachers-self-efficacy-personality-and-teaching-effective--28-czocher-ja-melhuish-k-kandasamy-ss-building-mathematics-self-efficacy-of-ness-a-meta-analysis-educ-res-rev-2014125976-httpdxdoiorg101016-stem-undergraduates-through-mathematical-modelling-internat-j-math-ed-sci). The curriculum traditionally emphasizes a systematic mastery of content and a high degree of logical rigor. While AI offers transformative advantages— such as the visualization of abstract dynamic geometry and automated reasoning—its implementation within Chinese MTES programs faces specific disciplinary challenges.

A primary tension exists between the exploratory nature of AI and the precision demanded by the national mathematics curriculum. As noted by Jiang et al. \[[9\]](#6-conclusion), the adoption of technology among Chinese student teachers is often pragmatic, frequently dictated by the need to balance innovative pedagogy with examination-oriented performance. Consequently, AI is often utilized for efficiency-based tasks, such as au- tomated grading or lesson planning, rather than for fostering high-order heuristic thinking. Understanding how MTES reconcile their profes- sional identities as ‘‘gatekeepers of rigor’’ with the affordances of AI

However, the analysis shows that there is no significant difference in AI-TPACK readiness across different grades of MTES. This finding is unexpected because one would typically expect senior or graduate students to possess more advanced technological skills \[[43\]](#11-klassen-rm-tze-vm-teachers-self-efficacy-personality-and-teaching-effective--28-czocher-ja-melhuish-k-kandasamy-ss-building-mathematics-self-efficacy-of-ness-a-meta-analysis-educ-res-rev-2014125976-httpdxdoiorg101016-stem-undergraduates-through-mathematical-modelling-internat-j-math-ed-sci). The data suggest that while graduate studies may improve a student’s confidence and refine their general teaching philosophies, they do not necessarily lead to a corresponding growth in AI-specific pedagogical knowledge. This lack of progress across academic levels can be attributed to the way AI knowledge is currently acquired. Most MTES rely on in- dependent internet-based learning, which tends to be fragmented and unsystematic. This informal approach makes it difficult to synthesize technical knowledge with specific mathematical content and pedagogy. Furthermore, the limited exposure to AI tools during teaching intern- ships indicates that secondary schools still largely adhere to traditional methods. This environment provides few opportunities for student teachers to practice and refine their AI-TPACK in real classrooms. With- out a structured and progressive curriculum that explicitly connects AI technology with mathematical instruction, students are likely to remain at a similar level of proficiency throughout their university

Second, teacher education must prioritize the psychological readi- ness of MTES. Since our SEM analysis confirms that self-efficacy is a robust positive predictor of AI-TPACK readiness, training should provide more positive experiences. By allowing MTES to design and im- plement short AI-enhanced mathematics micro-lessons in a supportive environment, programs can build the professional confidence necessary for future classroom integration.

Third, the curriculum must address the cognitive barrier identified in our structural model. A key finding of this study is that strong tradi- tional teaching beliefs are negatively associated with AI-TPACK readi- ness. This suggests that simply teaching technical skills is insufficient. Teacher educators should design ‘‘pedagogical reflection’’ workshops where MTES can discuss the tension between traditional procedural mastery and AI-augmented exploration. By showing how AI can ac- tually support mathematical rigor, we can help pre-service teachers reconcile their personal values with new technological possibilities. Finally, the lack of significant differences across grade levels sug- gests that AI-TPACK development should be a continuous thread. Rather than a single elective course, AI-related pedagogical train- ing should be embedded throughout the four-year curriculum, from introductory education theory to final teaching internships. This lon- gitudinal approach would ensure a more progressive development of the competencies required for the AI era.

## 6. Conclusion

This study clarifies the structural and psychological architecture of AI-TPACK readiness among MTES in China. By developing a domain- specific assessment tool and testing an exploratory structural model, we have identified that readiness is a complex synthesis of technical pro- ficiency, pedagogical alignment, and internal confidence. The strength of this research lies in its empirical validation of a multi-dimensional framework that bridges the gap between AI knowledge and psycho- logical readiness. These contributions provide a robust foundation for future research and policy-making in mathematics teacher education. The findings reveal that while MTES possess a moderate level of AI- TPACK, their application of AI remains at a preliminary stage, primarily focused on rudimentary tools rather than sophisticated, mathematics- specific systems. The lack of significant differences across grade levels suggests that current teacher education curricula may not yet be suf- ficiently tailored to promote a progressive development of AI-related competencies. Furthermore, the structural equation model provides a nuanced understanding of the determinants of readiness, indicating that while self-efficacy is a vital catalyst, strong traditional teaching beliefs can paradoxically impede the advancement of AI-TPACK.

## 7. Limitations and future research

Despite the theoretical and practical contributions, this study has several limitations that should be addressed in future research. First, the use of cross-sectional survey data limits our ability to establish definitive causal relationships within the structural model. The pathways identified between self-efficacy, beliefs, and AI-TPACK should be viewed as correlational, and future longitudinal studies are needed to track how these competencies evolve as MTES transition into professional teaching.

Second, the generalizability of the findings is primarily restricted to the mathematics teacher education context in China. Given the unique high-stakes and rigor-oriented nature of the Chinese curriculum, these results may not be directly applicable to other disciplines or cultural 

settings.

Third, the reliance on self-reported measures introduces the po- tential for social desirability bias, where participants may overstate their technical readiness. Future research would benefit from incor- porating multiple data modalities, such as classroom observations or performance-based assessments, to triangulate these findings.

Finally, the model modifications, specifically the pruning of non- significant paths, were conducted to achieve model parsimony within this specific cohort. While theoretically grounded in the specific context of this study, these modifications are exploratory. These adjustments should be considered exploratory, and further validation with larger, more diverse samples is required to confirm the stability of the model.
